questions.question: Describe the role of missionaries and traders on the northern frontier.
questions.expected_answer: Missionaries (LMS from 1795, also Methodists, Paris Evangelical, Glasgow, German and others) spread Christianity and set up schools; translated the Bible and created written forms of African languages; introduced crops, tools, irrigation, building methods and some medical care; acted as interpreters, advisers and go-betweens; some campaigned for indigenous rights (John Philip). Traders travelled north with wagons, trading goods for ivory, skins and cattle; missions became trading centres and bases for hunters and explorers. Chiefs welcomed missionaries for practical benefits but resisted changes to customs (polygamy, initiation, rainmaking, lobola).

questions.question: Describe Robert Moffat's work at Kuruman.
questions.expected_answer: Born 1795 in Scotland, gardener, LMS missionary, arrived 1817; converted Jager Afrikaner in Namaqualand; married Mary Smith (1819); joined the Batlhaping mission in 1821; called Griqua help at Dithakong (1823); moved the mission to the Kuruman Eye (1824); dug irrigation furrows for gardens, fruit trees and wheat; built a stone church (1838) and school; learnt Setswana with Tswana help, developed its written form, translated Luke (1830), New Testament (1840), full Bible (1857); printing press printed Bibles, hymns, school books; wrote Missionary Labours (1842); Kuruman became a base for travellers incl. Livingstone (married Mary Moffat 1845); friend of Mzilikazi; left 1870, died 1883.

questions.question: Evaluate Robert Moffat's legacy.
questions.expected_answer: Positive: Setswana Bible helped standardise written Setswana and spread literacy; school and printing press; irrigation and agriculture; peacemaker and diplomat (Mzilikazi, Mothibi); Kuruman mission is a heritage site. Critical: believed European culture superior, opposed rainmakers and healers, encouraged changes in dress and family life that disrupted Tswana society; missions opened the interior to traders, hunters and colonial expansion. Balanced view: complex figure; African interpreters, teachers and converts also shaped how Christianity was received.
